classification.difficultyReason: Identify matching angles in overlapping triangles, establish similarity and use corresponding sides to prove a product identity.

content.prompt: $AB$ and $DC$ are the parallel sides of a trapezium and are of such length that when diagonal $DB$ is constructed, $\angle DAB=\angle DBC$. Prove that $AB\times BC=DB\times AD$.

answer.short:
$AB\times BC=DB\times AD$.

Use $\triangle ABD\sim\triangle BDC$ (AAA), then equate corresponding-side ratios.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAD=\angle DBC$ (given), and $\angle ABD=\angle BDC$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DC$). The remaining angles are equal by the angle sum of a triangle. Hence $\triangle ABD\sim\triangle BDC$ (AAA).

Matching sides give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{DB}&=\frac{AD}{BC}\\AB\times BC&=DB\times AD.\end{align*}$$
